newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-REAL WARM UP FOR EAGERLY-ANTICIPATED BARCELONA CLASH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-REAL WARM UP FOR EAGERLY-ANTICIPATED BARCELONA CLASH.

text.p: After a weekend of hectic top-of-the-table action Spanish fans are already eagerly anticipating the December 7 clash between old rivals Real Madrid and Barcelona.
Just three weeks ago most commentators saw the championship developing into a one-horse race as a Barcelona side powered by Brazilian marksman Ronaldo steamrollered the opposition
But while Bobby Robson's team have let valuable points slip away, rivals Real have hit top form to go top.
"I'm looking forward to Barcelona's visit," Real president Lorenzo Sanz said after Sunday's 4-2 win over Valencia. "Spectacular play has arrived at the Bernabeu stadium."
Coach Fabio Capello, who had come under fire for using negative tactics, was also understandably happy with the result.
"You can't ask for more than that," he said. "I haven't even thought of Barcelona for a second."
Someone who is thinking of Barcelona is Croatian striker Davor Suker, scorer of a fine hat-trick against Valencia.

It has escaped nobody's notice in Spain that Suker's 12 goals have put him within one strike of Ronaldo. But the jovial Suker says he will happily give up the trophy for top goalscorer to Ronaldo, provided Real win the league.

Ronaldo had a quiet game in Saturday's 2-1 defeat at Athletic Bilbao, Barcelona's first of the season. The Brazilian and several other key players will be rested by coach Robson in Tuesday's friendly at Scotland's Celtic.

"The defeat is not something worrying," said former England manager Robson, who must find replacements for suspended players Josep Guardiola and Sergi Barjuan for Barcelona's next game against bottom-placed Extremadura.

Another British coach, former Liverpool striker John Toshack, saw his Deportivo Coruna side close to within one point of Barcelona and establish themselves as the only serious threat to the Real-Barcelona duopoly.
With Real Betis fourth, the top places in the Spanish league reflect fairly exactly the multi-billion peseta close-season outlay made by the respective clubs.
However, the only other teams which seem to be in with an outside chance of lifting the title stand out by shunning the transfer market.

Former France international Luis Fernandez has brought fallen giants Athletic Bilbao side up to fifth place despite the Basque club's policy of signing only players from the region, while Radomir Antic says he will not look for reinforcements for eighth-placed Atletico Madrid when the transfer market reopens in December.
